top.title: Stephen A. Smith says Giants HC John Harbaugh ‘should be ashamed’ after what he’s just heard
top.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images The New York Giants suffered a substantial defeat on Thursday night against their NFC East rivals, the Washington Commanders, in the race for the division. Although the Giants will end this week’s round of games still at the top of the NFC East, the game at MetLife Stadium should be viewed as a massive missed opportunity to take control of the division. Instead, the Giants have left the door open for the Dallas Cowboys to close the gap at the top. John Harbaugh was brought to the Giants in the offseason to help the Giants in the NFC East, but Thursday night’s game showed signs of the old Giants from years gone by. Stephen A. Smith was left far from impressed with what he saw at MetLife Stadium, and he took his frustration out on the veteran head coach. Stephen A. Smith unleashes on New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh Fortunately for the Giants , the Cowboys will be facing the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, but an unexpected victory could galvanise Brian Schottenheimer’s team heading into the final months of the season. “I mean, John Harbaugh should be ashamed of himself. That’s really what this is,” Smith said on First Take. “The point that I’m making is this: John Harbaugh, this is not new. This is one of the problems that existed in Baltimore, in terms of being a bit outdated. Coming across as a bit, okay, of course he knows what he’s doing in terms of being a football coach overall. Of course he knows how to lead. He’s been there forever, he’s been in the NFL, we understand and have nothing but profound respect, he’s a Super Bowl champion, we get all of that. “But on too many occasions, you’re coaching scared. Which is why, what is the number, Shay, right now? 47 fourth-quarter blown leads in his career over the last decade-plus? I mean, that’s just embarrassing.” The statistic shared by Smith certainly does not reflect well on Harbaugh. The Giants have brought in a former Super Bowl winner, but he clearly has a track record of blowing the lead in the fourth quarter. Something worth keeping in mind is the Giants’ run of fixtures following what should have been a comfortable win over a struggling Commanders team. Before the end of the season, the Giants still have to play Jacksonville, San Francisco, Seattle, Cleveland, Detroit and Dallas. Granted, the Giants still hold the lead in the division, but the game on Thursday was an almost-certain victory that they have thrown away. Perhaps Harbaugh and the Giants were looking beyond Thursday’s game at some of the more difficult tests coming up over the coming weeks. It has certainly come back to bite them. top.title: Big stadiums v small stadiums - which is better?
top.description: [BBC] Each week we ask you for your opinions on one of the pressing topics concerning the Women's Super League. This time we are asking for your thoughts on clubs playing their matches in large grounds used by the men's sides. Is it better for women to play in big stadiums with empty seats or smaller stadiums where facilities are sometimes below par, but maybe where the more compact nature and smaller capacity makes for a better atmosphere? All of Chelsea's WSL games this season take place at Stamford Bridge after moving on from Kingsmeadow, while Arsenal have made Emirates Stadium their home having previously staged games at Borehamwood. Chelsea entertain WSL leaders Manchester City on Saturday, but the Blues had less than 6,000 watching at home against Everton last week. Arsenal have the highest attendance figures in the league, however their best attended league match in 2026-27, which saw 29,853 watch their game with Manchester United, was still played out at a half-empty Emirates. There are no men's matches this weekend, but Manchester United, Tottenham and West Ham are not hosting their WSL games at the men's sides stadiums, with United instead at Leigh, Tottenham at Leyton Orient and West Ham at Dagenham and Redbridge. However, the Aston Villa v Birmingham derby is at Villa Park and Brighton versus Liverpool is at American Express Stadium. What can be done to boost WSL attendances and atmospheres? top.title: Arsenal defender scores international brace playing out of position
top.description: Arsenal defender scores international brace playing out of position Jurrien Timber starred for the Netherlands playing at left-back on Friday night, scoring a brace in a win over Greece and Arsenal teammate Christos Tzolis. Photo by Clive Rose/Getty Images Arsenal teammates Jurrien Timber and Christos Tzolis faced off with their national teams on Friday, with the Netherlands taking on Greece in the Nations League. The two teams had made unbeaten starts to the group stage, winning two games and drawing two games each. But any hopes of a close contest were quickly extinguished by a dominant Netherlands display. Timber found himself playing at left-back, rather than his usual positions on the right or at centre-back. But he was still heavily involved in a free-scoring first half. Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images Timber played the pass before the goal for the Netherlands’ second and third goals of the half, which both came in the opening 20 minutes of the game. The Arsenal defender then scored a striker’s finish from close range in the 40th minute, to make it 5-0. But the goals didn’t stop at half-time, and Timber popped up at the back post for another tap-in for 6-0 in the 59th minute. With the Netherlands going on to score a seventh two minutes later, the game slowed down. The two teams made nine substitutions between them in the following 15 minutes, including the withdrawals of both Timber and Tzolis. The highlights are available here . From an Arsenal point of view, considering the two players have been injured recently, it was good to see neither had to complete the full 90. Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images Greece may have suffered a damaging blow to their confidence, but they still have a chance to progress to the knockouts. If they better Germany’s result in the final games, they’ll make the Nations League quarter-finals. The same is true if both teams draw or both lose. But if they both win, Germany will go through. Greece host Serbia on Monday, November 16th, 19:45 GMT, whilst Germany host the Netherlands at the same time. Greece will have to hope the Netherlands are just as ruthless against Germany. top.title: Refusing to Buy Defensive Cover in January Would Be Negligence That Will Cost Manchester City the Title
top.description: Refusing to Buy Defensive Cover in January Would Be Negligence That Will Cost Manchester City the Title Hugo Viana and co must strengthen Manchester City's backline in January. Since a 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain at the Etihad Stadium in October, players such as Marc Guehi, Gianluigi Donnarumma and Josko Gvardiol have struggled immensely, be it because of a lack of confidence or the concerning selection choices that Maresca is making far too often. The 46-year-old, having started life as Pep Guardiola’s successor perfectly with eight consecutive wins, has been subjected to intense scrutiny ahead of the November international break, mainly because of his tactical structure against Nottingham Forest . City lost 3-1 after Liam Delap twice capitalised on poor defending following Jair Cunha’s opening goal just six minutes into the contest at the City Ground. All three goals came from errors that were caused by Maresca’s decision to leave Elliot Anderson stranded deep in midfield, and at the same time, Enzo Fernandez was ordered to play higher up, in closer proximity to Rayan Cherki. It was a game in agonising need for someone like Ayyoub Bouaddi. The defeat was humbling in that Forest, who hadn’t scored a goal at home for 167 days, managed to claim victory and pile vast confusion amongst City supporters, who saw their side drop into third in the Premier League table behind leaders Arsenal and second-placed Brighton and Hove Albion . A drop in form has drawn a scroll of questions that need to be answered in the coming weeks if Maresca wants to regain belief in his side, and so too to receive backing from Manchester City supporters. So what’s the fix? Even in their struggles to put the ball into the back of the net at the top of the pitch, it’s clear that the main focus in the January transfer window for sporting director Hugo Viana and Maresca must be defenders. Shortly after completing the signing of Fernandez for a joint-British record fee of £125 million from Chelsea , Maresca said that the Argentine is “unbelievable around the box” , and it seems the Italian wants to play him higher up the pitch. This theory has led to reasonable anger as to why Maresca insists on playing him alongside Anderson in midfield, who, despite his unbelievable talent and work rate, simply cannot keep up with one, two, or three players attacking his box at once. These leaky defensive performances won’t fix themselves, but it would be naive to predict that Maresca is too stubborn to change his ways. The manager has found success at Leicester City and Chelsea, and will want to mirror that on a large scale, perhaps, in east Manchester. In some ways, Maresca needs to look at the 2024-25 season under Guardiola to realise that splashing big money on defenders may be more of a necessity than it is a desire. top.title: Maryland volleyball outlasted by Rutgers in five-set loss
top.description: Through 16 matches of Big Ten play, Maryland women’s volleyball’s attacking errors in tight sets have been the primary hurdle they’ve been unable to overcome versus conference competition. Against Rutgers on Friday night, that proved to be true once again. Despite out-killing the Scarlet Knights, 72-64, behind 65 assists from Sara Toth, Maryland lost 31 points on attack errors in a heartbreaking 3-2 road loss. Coming off a clean sweep defeat against Penn State on Wednesday, Maryland went into this match ready to defend its position in the Big Ten tournament. Maryland entered the game in 15th place, the last seed in the tournament, while the Scarlet Knights stood at 16th The teams knew it was an important night for them both, having come into this match struggling at 3-12 in the conference. The Terps established momentum by drawing the first blood of the night with a kill from star freshman Brooklynne Brass. Maryland continued to protect its lead in short, sporadic bursts as the set went on. Even as the set remained close, the Terps emerged with a .184 hitting percentage and took home the opening frame of the night, 26-24. Despite dropping the opening set, the Scarlet Knights restored their momentum just in time for the second set. In another thrilling set, both defenses went toe-to-toe, as seen by the close hitting percentages in this set. Even after Maryland built a 15-10 lead at the media timeout, three Terps service errors and a late 4-0 Scarlet Knights run allowed Rutgers to seal the frame, 25-22. In the third set, Rutgers won by the exact same score. It took a lead at 7-6 and didn’t trail after that, with the Terps putting up a meager .140 hitting percentage. The fourth set continued the neck-in-neck battle. After taking two consecutive sets, Rutgers wanted to carry its momentum into another successive set, but Maryland stayed relentless in its attempts to hang on. With a total of six ties, the set proved to be yet another close matchup for both teams. The Terps managed their way through a significant 5-1 run mid-set, a stretch that would remain consequential for their inevitable win. As hard as they tried, Rutgers couldn’t overcome that deficit — allowing Maryland to take their second set at 25-20. That victory propelled both teams into the ultimate five-set thriller. Unfazed by their most recent set loss, the Scarlet Knights sparked an immediate 4-1 burst.. But another kill from Brass took the Terps to their first lead of the fifth set. Yet, that hope was short-lived. With a kill from outside hitter Karis Willow, who spent the match executing at .333 clearance, Rutgers took home a final close set at 15-13 and won the match. Three things to know 1. Every point matters. In close matches like this, every point truly does matter. With both teams combining for 16 service errors on the night, seven from Maryland and nine from Rutgers, neither side could afford to give away free points with such small margins. 2. top.title: Rayan hands Manchester United open transfer invitation after making bold personal admission
top.description: Rayan hands Manchester United open transfer invitation after making bold personal admission What AFC Bournemouth’s Rayan has just confessed about the Cherries’ 3-0 win over Manchester United should set alarm bells ringing at Old Trafford. Last month, the Cherries travelled to Manchester and outwitted Michael Carrick ’s side, a statement victory that added to the misery of the embattled former United head coach. Weeks later, that win is still being discussed. In an interview alongside clubmate Evanilson for ESPN Brazil , as transcribed by Sport Witness , Rayan was asked how it felt to beat United. Rayan’s Manchester United confession He replied while making some interesting confessions: “Yeah, it’s true, that’s exactly how it feels. I was even talking to the people at home, my wife and the people who are with me, and I told them I’ve always supported Manchester United here in England.” The interviewer then asked whether, while still a Bournemouth player, he continues to follow United. “Yes, really,” he answered. When pressed on why, he added: “Because of Cristiano Ronaldo.” Rayan could have been a Manchester United player Hearing Rayan say this, and remembering that United could reportedly have signed him last winter ahead of Bournemouth, will frustrate Old Trafford supporters. But what has frustrated them further is how quickly he adapted to the Premier League. Rayan Premier League stats He arrived and immediately transferred his Vasco da Gama goalscoring form, finding the net five times in his first 15 games while providing two assists. His bright start prompted leading outlets to produce detailed analysis of his quality. The Athletic labelled him “already one of the Premier League’s most fearsome attackers”. The piece highlighted how perfectly he filled the void left by Antoine Semenyo, noting how decisive the now Manchester City forward had been for the Cherries. Big transfer boost All of this gives United perfect motivation to bring Rayan to Old Trafford. Should they find themselves in a race for his signature, he is likely to lean towards a move to M16. Favouring a switch to Manchester is one thing, however; meeting Bournemouth’s hefty asking price is quite another. The versatile Bournemouth star reportedly carries a £130 million release clause in his deal at the Vitality Stadium.

top.description: TAMPA, FL - MARCH 14: Christian Cairo #70 of the Philadelphia Phillies scores a run in the third inning during the game between the Philadelphia Phillies and the New York Yankees at George M. (Photo by Grace Hoppel/MLB Photos via Getty Images) MLB Photos via Getty Images The Los Angeles Dodgers have wasted little time getting their offseason roster work underway following another season at the top of the National League, but with a disappointing finish before the World Series. As the general manager meetings began this week in Las Vegas, the Dodgers announced an initial move, acquiring a player who appeared to be a promising piece of the Philadelphia Phillies’ future before joining their division rival, then being picked up by the Dodgers. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Mets $22 Million Castoff Sends ‘Crazy’ Message After Surprise Trade Los Angeles Dodgers Add Former Philadelphia Phillies Infielder On Monday, the Dodgers announced they had claimed infielder Christian Cairo shortly after he left the Phillies for the New York Mets. “The Dodgers claimed IF Christian Cairo from the New York Mets,” the team stated . Cairo, 25, has yet to make his major league debut despite spending several seasons working his way through professional baseball’s minor league system. His brief Mets stay represented another change of organizations after a lengthy stint with Philadelphia. “A career-long minor-leaguer who spent most of last year in the Philadelphia Phillies’ organization –– hitting .227 with a .676 OPS in 128 games with their triple-A affiliate –– Cairo was a late-season waiver addition for the Mets, who subsequently re-signed him to a one-year contract on a split MLB/minor-league deal earlier this month,” Jack Harris reported for the New York Post . The Phillies designated Cairo for assignment in September and the Mets subsequently claimed him off waivers before eventually designating him for assignment themselves on November 2, despite the new contract. The Dodgers have now stepped in to claim the infielder, giving him another opportunity to continue his professional career with a new organization. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Cubs’ $68 Million Starter Castoff Jameson Taillon Makes Return Announcement What Christian Cairo Could Bring To Los Angeles Dodgers After Philadelphia Phillies Exit Cairo offers some positional flexibility that could make him useful as organizational depth. He has experience at second base, shortstop and third base, while also seeing action in the outfield during his minor league career. Cairo recorded 25 stolen bases in 2026 and drew more walks than strikeouts during his minor league campaign. Those abilities could give Los Angeles another versatile option to evaluate heading into spring training. top.title: FA Cup test for the Welsh side aiming for WSL 2
top.description: Gwalia United are unbeaten in nine games in all competitions but face a stern challenge this weekend [Benjamin Brain Photography] For a club with ambitions of reaching the Women's Super League's second tier (WSL 2) by 2030, Gwalia United's relegation last season to the fourth tier of English women's football looks a significant setback. Yet there is a belief at the Welsh club that taking one step in the wrong direction can ultimately help take them forward. This Sunday (14:00 GMT) brings the chance for Gwalia to show they are making progress once more, as they target an upset against Oxford United in the Women's FA Cup second round. The U's are top of the division Gwalia dropped out of last season, and so are within sight of WSL 2. In short, they are where Gwalia want to be, and will start as favourites to seal a round-three place at USW Sport Park. Yet for Gwalia, the cup brings a chance for what would be a statement victory. "It takes a lot of pressure off us because people from the outside looking in probably don't expect us to do a lot," says captain Cerys Jones "It's a good opportunity to challenge ourselves." Relegation 'hit us hard' Gwalia will have beaten AFC Stoneham and Yate Town in this season's Women's FA Cup [Benjamin Brain Photography] Gwalia, who were formerly known as Cardiff City Ladies, have a proud history of developing Welsh talent. Stars such as Jess Fishlock, Sophie Ingle, Ffion Morgan, Gemma Evans and Lily Woodham played for the club before going on to represent Wales. And after co-owners Julian Jenkins and Canva founder Damien Singh got involved before the 2024-25 season, there was hope of keeping some of that emerging talent within Wales while allowing Gwalia to compete at a higher level. However, making progress has not been easy, even if last season's relegation from the Southern Premier Division was the result of fine margins. Gwalia finished with the same goal difference as AFC Wimbledon, but were relegated as the London club had scored one more goal. "It hit us hard, it really did," says manager Cori Williams-Mills. Gwalia are currently fourth in Division One South West, having lost only one of their eight league games so far this season. The average age of the squad is just 20, and Williams-Mills believes her youthful team can not only return to the third tier but go on to reach new heights. "When we get back up, we'll be better equipped than we would have been if we'd stayed [up]," she adds. "Sometimes taking a step back can help push you further forward. "We ended last year a little disappointed. This season, the girls have been excellent. "Is it going to take us time to get where we want to be? Is it going to be hard along the way? Yeah, of course it is, but we'll get there." top.title: Mancini has three key Italy line-up doubts for Belgium clash as Cambiaghi trains separately
top.description: Mancini has three key Italy line-up doubts for Belgium clash as Cambiaghi trains separately Sky Sport Italia reports that Nicolò Cambiaghi trained separately this morning, so Federico Dimarco could replace him against Belgium, but coach Roberto Mancini has two more line-up doubts. Italy visit Belgium on Sunday for the final Nations League group-stage game. The Azzurri are currently the Group A1 leaders, level on 10 points with France, but with a better head-to-head record. Belgium sit third with nine points, while Turkiye have already been relegated to the second division, with five defeats from five. Italy team news: Cambiaghi trains separately & Mancini’s doubts MILAN – NOVEMBER 12: Nicolo Cambiaghi of Italy is challenged by Malo Gusto and Dayot Upamecano of France during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Italy and France at San Siro Stadium on November 12, 2026 in Milan. (Photo by Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images) Italy trained at the Inter training centre this morning, before flying to Brussels in the afternoon. Sky Sport reports that Cambiaghi trained separately, so if he’s not fit enough to start, or even be available tomorrow, Dimarco will feature in the Azzurri XI instead as a left winger. Mancini’s other doubt is on the right flank, with either Vergara or Sebastiano Esposito starting. top.title: “It’s Disgusting”: Craig Carton Slams Kirk Herbstreit for Feeding Steak to His Dog at NYC Restaurant
top.description: Kirk Herbstreit gives some love to his dog, Peter. © USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Kirk Herbstreit’s recent outing with his dog Peter has sparked controversy. The ESPN college football analyst shared a video of his dog enjoying a steak at a New York City restaurant. While the moment seemed cute to Herbstreit, sports commentator Craig Carton was not happy about it. He questioned the decision to bring a dog into a steakhouse and feed it a meal meant for humans. Herbstreit posted a video of himself cutting a steak and placing the pieces in front of Peter. The golden retriever wasted no time in finishing the meal, eating an entire plate of cut-up steak in less than 17 seconds. “Petey got into another steak in NYC last night… I wish he would enjoy it,” Herbstreit wrote. However, Carton reacted very differently when discussing the video on his show. “I’m not anti-dog. I just don’t want to go to a steakhouse and eat next to a dog. Because it’s disgusting,” Carton said. He went on to criticize Herbstreit for documenting the experience and questioned why the analyst would serve an expensive steak to his dog while dining with his wife and friends. “‘I love my dog more than you love your dog. You look to your right, and a beautifully cooked medium-rare steak is delivered to the Herbstreit table, but it’s not for any of the adults at that table, it’s for his dog. And Kirk, on camera now, because you’ve got to document everything you do, God forbid you act like a human being and you don’t film every aspect of your life – in a New York City steakhouse,” he added. According to Carton, other customers expecting a quiet meal may have been disturbed by a dog sitting next to them. He spread his love across the country and so many of you welcomed him into your lives. We miss him every day and are so appreciative of his spirit that blessed so many lives for the 10 years he was alive. Love you Benny,” Herbstreit wrote. The tribute received an outpouring of affection from fans. Many remembered Ben fondly, while others showered the dog with praise. nigeria.title: How lifestyle, late detection fuel diabetes crisis in Nigeria
nigeria.description: As Nigeria joins the rest of the world to commemorate World Diabetes Day(WDD), marked annually on Nov. 14, health experts have warned that changing lifestyles and late detection are fuelling a diabetes crisis in the country. WDD is commemorated to raise awareness on prevention, early detection and care. Diabetes Mellitus, a chronic metabolic condition characterised by elevated blood sugar due to inability of the pancreas to produce enough insulin or impaired insulin action, has become a major public health concern, with complications including blindness, kidney failure, heart failure, stroke and limb amputation. According to the International Diabetes Federation (IDF) Diabetes Atlas, globally no fewer than 589 million adults live with diabetes, with 24.6 million in Africa. About 11 million adults live with the condition in Nigeria, with many unaware of their status. Experts said the disease, which could remain undetected for years without symptoms, was now killing more Nigerians than malaria, HIV and tuberculosis combined. An Endocrinologist, Prof. Michael Olamoyegun, said diabetes killed more Nigerians than malaria, HIV and tuberculosis combined. Olamoyegun is Professor of Medicine and Endocrinology at Ladoke Akintola University of Technology and also Consultant Physician and Endocrinologist at LAUTECH Teaching Hospital, Ogbomoso, Oyo State. He said diabetes is a metabolic disorder of carbohydrates, fats and protein. He added that it is characterised by elevated blood sugar due to inability of pancreas to produce enough insulin. According to him, diabetes also occurs if insulin action is impaired. He said there are many variants but three main types existed – Type 1, Type 2 and Gestational Diabetes. ” Type 1 diabetes, which occurs due to absolute deficiency of insulin, is seen mainly in younger age group, usually less than 30 years, although occasionally in adulthood. “It is found in about five to ten per cent of all individuals with diabetes. “This group is managed with insulin injections since the body no longer produces insulin.” The endocrinologist said Type 2 diabetes represented 90 to 95 per cent of individuals with diabetes, stressing it occurred when insulin was not able to function well in the body. He also noted that it usually occurred in older individuals who had family history in first-degree relatives. Olamoyegun, also the Secretary General of the Association of Clinical Endocrinologists of Nigeria (ACEN), added that hypertension, overweight or obesity and sedentary lifestyles were contributory risk factors. He said it is usually managed with oral medications, dietary control and occasionally with insulin. On gestational diabetes mellitus, he said it was first detected in pregnancy, saying it complicated about 7.5 to 12 per cent of all pregnancies. nigeria.title: Airspace Now ‘Opened Up,’ No Cyberattack — US
nigeria.description: The United States on Friday lifted an hours-long ground stop at the nation’s airports, with top officials explaining that the disruption was due to old equipment and not a cyberattack or sweeping Microsoft outage. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told a late-night briefing at the White House that US airspace was now “opened up,” while warning it would take time for the travel chaos to clear. “At 8:15 tonight Eastern Time, we’ve opened up the airspace,” Duffy said. “Now does that mean every flight is going to fly right now? It’s going to be slow.” Passengers wait for updates at a check-in area at Terminal 7 at Los Angeles International Airport, in Los Angeles on November 13, 2026. US aviation regulators issued an extremely rare ground stop of all flights across the country on November 13 after a major communications outage which the Department of Homeland Security said did not appear to be the result of any “nefarious attack.” The breakdown came a day after Duffy and the White House had formally asked Congress for $30 billion to upgrade and modernize the US Air Traffic Control System. “Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data, and they went down,” Duffy said. “It’s the old hardware that went down, and I think the question for the American people is: Do you want your Congress to fund this?” Duffy, however, insisted it was still safe for Americans to fly. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin dismissed speculation about a coordinated cyber assault on the United States, or any link to the Microsoft outage that affected services worldwide. “Welcome to Friday the 13th, right? You know, I want to make sure everybody understands that there is no connection between this and Microsoft. I know a lot of people are making that jump,” Mullin said. Mullin added there was “actually no cyber attack.” “When we start looking at cyber threats, cyber attacks, typically some people are going to raise their hand up and say, ‘Hey, we did that.’ There’s no chatter.’ We haven’t seen any footprints,” he added. But he said US security and law enforcement agencies were still checking and had ruled nothing out. Passengers wait in line to retrieve their luggage as flights were cancelled at Chicago O’Hare International Airport in Chicago on November 13, 2026. The two officials also defended President Donald Trump, who had yet to comment on the air stoppage some five hours after it began. “President Trump immediately had people in his office,” Mullin said. “We were communicating.” Passengers wait at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, Washington, DC on November 13, 2026. Sworn in at the New Jersey Statehouse in Trenton on 9 November 2026, Emehelu has made double history in the process—becoming New Jersey’s first immigrant Lieutenant Governor and forming part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Born in Nigeria before moving to the United States at the age of three, Emehelu brings an extraordinary record of public service and legal excellence to New Jersey’s second-highest executive office. Before this historic appointment, she served as Acting State Comptroller , leading key efforts to combat fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting taxpayer funds and strengthening government accountability, and also stepped in as Acting Secretary of State to oversee New Jersey’s elections. Her public sector résumé also includes a two-year tenure as Executive Assistant Attorney General of New Jersey, where she served as the third-ranking official in the New Jersey Attorney General’s Office. entertainment.title: FWIFT 2026 Convention Communique: Industry Leaders Charge Women in Media to Embrace Cross-Border Growth
entertainment.description: The Forum for Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) successfully concluded its 2026 annual convention on Thursday, October 29, at the historic Glover Memorial Hall in Lagos, Nigeria. Convening under the theme “One Industry, Many Voices: Building Together,” the afternoon brought together over 200 practitioners from several sectors including; film, television, radio, advertising, and digital media to connect, share insights, and build mutual agency. Supported by the African Women’s Development Fund (AWDF) , the convention featured a keynote address by cultural curator Sandra Mbanefo Obiago , interactive panel sessions, break-out workshops, speed networking, and a flagship fireside chat titled “The Cross Over: A Career Beyond Borders.” The event drew leading voices from across the creative economy, including media executive Kadaria Ahmed , filmmaker Biodun Stephens, media personality Gbemi Olateru-Olagbegi, executive director Rosemary Egabor-Afolahan, and director Esosa Osagiede. Key takeaways and actionable resolutions from the convention sessions emphasized resilience, strategic partnerships, and structural evolution: Embrace Bold Collaboration and Risk-Taking: Speakers urged media professionals to shed apprehension around institutional partnerships. As highlighted during the panel discussions: “Do not allow fear of failing stop you from asking for help, do your due diligence on the people you want to partner with then go for it. If it does not work, do not stop, get up and go again.” Adaptability as a Survival Imperative: In an era of rapid technological and digital shifts across broadcast and film, participants were reminded of the absolute necessity of evolution: “If you don’t change with the times, you will grow stale.” Deconstructing Industry Myths: Addressing professional dynamics, panelists challenged antiquated narratives regarding female competition, affirming that systemic progress relies on solidarity: “Women work well with women, it is a myth that they do not.” FWIFT’s leadership noted that the conversations at Glover Memorial Hall mark a critical step toward cementing cross-sector alliances. The forum remains committed to translating these insights into actionable frameworks, mentorship programs, and policy advocacy for women shaping the future of African media. For more information on upcoming FWIFT initiatives, programs, and future events, visit the official website or follow @fwiftnigeria on social media. entertainment.title: Ayobami Esther Akinnagbe: Organisational Mistakes Start-up Founders Should Avoid
entertainment.description: Two women engaged in a professional meeting, discussing business in a modern office setting. Image by RDNE Stock project for Pexels . There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. sports.title: Stephen A. Smith says Giants HC John Harbaugh ‘should be ashamed’ after what he’s just heard
sports.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images The New York Giants suffered a substantial defeat on Thursday night against their NFC East rivals, the Washington Commanders, in the race for the division. Although the Giants will end this week’s round of games still at the top of the NFC East, the game at MetLife Stadium should be viewed as a massive missed opportunity to take control of the division. Instead, the Giants have left the door open for the Dallas Cowboys to close the gap at the top. John Harbaugh was brought to the Giants in the offseason to help the Giants in the NFC East, but Thursday night’s game showed signs of the old Giants from years gone by. Stephen A. Smith was left far from impressed with what he saw at MetLife Stadium, and he took his frustration out on the veteran head coach. Stephen A. Smith unleashes on New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh Fortunately for the Giants , the Cowboys will be facing the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, but an unexpected victory could galvanise Brian Schottenheimer’s team heading into the final months of the season. “I mean, John Harbaugh should be ashamed of himself. That’s really what this is,” Smith said on First Take. “The point that I’m making is this: John Harbaugh, this is not new. This is one of the problems that existed in Baltimore, in terms of being a bit outdated. Coming across as a bit, okay, of course he knows what he’s doing in terms of being a football coach overall. Of course he knows how to lead. He’s been there forever, he’s been in the NFL, we understand and have nothing but profound respect, he’s a Super Bowl champion, we get all of that. “But on too many occasions, you’re coaching scared. Which is why, what is the number, Shay, right now? 47 fourth-quarter blown leads in his career over the last decade-plus? I mean, that’s just embarrassing.” The statistic shared by Smith certainly does not reflect well on Harbaugh. The Giants have brought in a former Super Bowl winner, but he clearly has a track record of blowing the lead in the fourth quarter. Something worth keeping in mind is the Giants’ run of fixtures following what should have been a comfortable win over a struggling Commanders team. Before the end of the season, the Giants still have to play Jacksonville, San Francisco, Seattle, Cleveland, Detroit and Dallas. This time we are asking for your thoughts on clubs playing their matches in large grounds used by the men's sides. sports.title: Arsenal defender scores international brace playing out of position
sports.description: Arsenal defender scores international brace playing out of position Jurrien Timber starred for the Netherlands playing at left-back on Friday night, scoring a brace in a win over Greece and Arsenal teammate Christos Tzolis. Photo by Clive Rose/Getty Images Arsenal teammates Jurrien Timber and Christos Tzolis faced off with their national teams on Friday, with the Netherlands taking on Greece in the Nations League. The two teams had made unbeaten starts to the group stage, winning two games and drawing two games each. But any hopes of a close contest were quickly extinguished by a dominant Netherlands display. Timber found himself playing at left-back, rather than his usual positions on the right or at centre-back. But he was still heavily involved in a free-scoring first half. Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images Timber played the pass before the goal for the Netherlands’ second and third goals of the half, which both came in the opening 20 minutes of the game. The Arsenal defender then scored a striker’s finish from close range in the 40th minute, to make it 5-0. But the goals didn’t stop at half-time, and Timber popped up at the back post for another tap-in for 6-0 in the 59th minute. With the Netherlands going on to score a seventh two minutes later, the game slowed down. The two teams made nine substitutions between them in the following 15 minutes, including the withdrawals of both Timber and Tzolis. The highlights are available here . From an Arsenal point of view, considering the two players have been injured recently, it was good to see neither had to complete the full 90. Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images Greece may have suffered a damaging blow to their confidence, but they still have a chance to progress to the knockouts. If they better Germany’s result in the final games, they’ll make the Nations League quarter-finals. The same is true if both teams draw or both lose. But if they both win, Germany will go through. Greece host Serbia on Monday, November 16th, 19:45 GMT, whilst Germany host the Netherlands at the same time. Greece will have to hope the Netherlands are just as ruthless against Germany. sports.description: Refusing to Buy Defensive Cover in January Would Be Negligence That Will Cost Manchester City the Title Hugo Viana and co must strengthen Manchester City's backline in January. Since a 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain at the Etihad Stadium in October, players such as Marc Guehi, Gianluigi Donnarumma and Josko Gvardiol have struggled immensely, be it because of a lack of confidence or the concerning selection choices that Maresca is making far too often. The 46-year-old, having started life as Pep Guardiola’s successor perfectly with eight consecutive wins, has been subjected to intense scrutiny ahead of the November international break, mainly because of his tactical structure against Nottingham Forest . City lost 3-1 after Liam Delap twice capitalised on poor defending following Jair Cunha’s opening goal just six minutes into the contest at the City Ground. All three goals came from errors that were caused by Maresca’s decision to leave Elliot Anderson stranded deep in midfield, and at the same time, Enzo Fernandez was ordered to play higher up, in closer proximity to Rayan Cherki. It was a game in agonising need for someone like Ayyoub Bouaddi. The defeat was humbling in that Forest, who hadn’t scored a goal at home for 167 days, managed to claim victory and pile vast confusion amongst City supporters, who saw their side drop into third in the Premier League table behind leaders Arsenal and second-placed Brighton and Hove Albion . A drop in form has drawn a scroll of questions that need to be answered in the coming weeks if Maresca wants to regain belief in his side, and so too to receive backing from Manchester City supporters. This theory has led to reasonable anger as to why Maresca insists on playing him alongside Anderson in midfield, who, despite his unbelievable talent and work rate, simply cannot keep up with one, two, or three players attacking his box at once. sports.title: Maryland volleyball outlasted by Rutgers in five-set loss
sports.description: Through 16 matches of Big Ten play, Maryland women’s volleyball’s attacking errors in tight sets have been the primary hurdle they’ve been unable to overcome versus conference competition. Against Rutgers on Friday night, that proved to be true once again. Despite out-killing the Scarlet Knights, 72-64, behind 65 assists from Sara Toth, Maryland lost 31 points on attack errors in a heartbreaking 3-2 road loss. Coming off a clean sweep defeat against Penn State on Wednesday, Maryland went into this match ready to defend its position in the Big Ten tournament. Maryland entered the game in 15th place, the last seed in the tournament, while the Scarlet Knights stood at 16th The teams knew it was an important night for them both, having come into this match struggling at 3-12 in the conference. The Terps established momentum by drawing the first blood of the night with a kill from star freshman Brooklynne Brass. Maryland continued to protect its lead in short, sporadic bursts as the set went on. Even as the set remained close, the Terps emerged with a .184 hitting percentage and took home the opening frame of the night, 26-24. Despite dropping the opening set, the Scarlet Knights restored their momentum just in time for the second set. In another thrilling set, both defenses went toe-to-toe, as seen by the close hitting percentages in this set. Even after Maryland built a 15-10 lead at the media timeout, three Terps service errors and a late 4-0 Scarlet Knights run allowed Rutgers to seal the frame, 25-22. In the third set, Rutgers won by the exact same score. It took a lead at 7-6 and didn’t trail after that, with the Terps putting up a meager .140 hitting percentage. The fourth set continued the neck-in-neck battle. After taking two consecutive sets, Rutgers wanted to carry its momentum into another successive set, but Maryland stayed relentless in its attempts to hang on. With a total of six ties, the set proved to be yet another close matchup for both teams. As hard as they tried, Rutgers couldn’t overcome that deficit — allowing Maryland to take their second set at 25-20. That victory propelled both teams into the ultimate five-set thriller. Unfazed by their most recent set loss, the Scarlet Knights sparked an immediate 4-1 burst.. But another kill from Brass took the Terps to their first lead of the fifth set. sports.title: Rayan hands Manchester United open transfer invitation after making bold personal admission
sports.description: Rayan hands Manchester United open transfer invitation after making bold personal admission What AFC Bournemouth’s Rayan has just confessed about the Cherries’ 3-0 win over Manchester United should set alarm bells ringing at Old Trafford. Last month, the Cherries travelled to Manchester and outwitted Michael Carrick ’s side, a statement victory that added to the misery of the embattled former United head coach. Weeks later, that win is still being discussed. In an interview alongside clubmate Evanilson for ESPN Brazil , as transcribed by Sport Witness , Rayan was asked how it felt to beat United. Rayan’s Manchester United confession He replied while making some interesting confessions: “Yeah, it’s true, that’s exactly how it feels. I was even talking to the people at home, my wife and the people who are with me, and I told them I’ve always supported Manchester United here in England.” The interviewer then asked whether, while still a Bournemouth player, he continues to follow United. “Yes, really,” he answered. When pressed on why, he added: “Because of Cristiano Ronaldo.” Rayan could have been a Manchester United player Hearing Rayan say this, and remembering that United could reportedly have signed him last winter ahead of Bournemouth, will frustrate Old Trafford supporters. But what has frustrated them further is how quickly he adapted to the Premier League. Rayan Premier League stats He arrived and immediately transferred his Vasco da Gama goalscoring form, finding the net five times in his first 15 games while providing two assists. His bright start prompted leading outlets to produce detailed analysis of his quality. The Athletic labelled him “already one of the Premier League’s most fearsome attackers”. The piece highlighted how perfectly he filled the void left by Antoine Semenyo, noting how decisive the now Manchester City forward had been for the Cherries. Big transfer boost All of this gives United perfect motivation to bring Rayan to Old Trafford. Should they find themselves in a race for his signature, he is likely to lean towards a move to M16. Favouring a switch to Manchester is one thing, however; meeting Bournemouth’s hefty asking price is quite another. The versatile Bournemouth star reportedly carries a £130 million release clause in his deal at the Vitality Stadium.

sports.description: Gwalia United are unbeaten in nine games in all competitions but face a stern challenge this weekend [Benjamin Brain Photography] For a club with ambitions of reaching the Women's Super League's second tier (WSL 2) by 2030, Gwalia United's relegation last season to the fourth tier of English women's football looks a significant setback. Yet there is a belief at the Welsh club that taking one step in the wrong direction can ultimately help take them forward. This Sunday (14:00 GMT) brings the chance for Gwalia to show they are making progress once more, as they target an upset against Oxford United in the Women's FA Cup second round. The U's are top of the division Gwalia dropped out of last season, and so are within sight of WSL 2. In short, they are where Gwalia want to be, and will start as favourites to seal a round-three place at USW Sport Park. Yet for Gwalia, the cup brings a chance for what would be a statement victory. "It takes a lot of pressure off us because people from the outside looking in probably don't expect us to do a lot," says captain Cerys Jones "It's a good opportunity to challenge ourselves." Relegation 'hit us hard' Gwalia will have beaten AFC Stoneham and Yate Town in this season's Women's FA Cup [Benjamin Brain Photography] Gwalia, who were formerly known as Cardiff City Ladies, have a proud history of developing Welsh talent. Stars such as Jess Fishlock, Sophie Ingle, Ffion Morgan, Gemma Evans and Lily Woodham played for the club before going on to represent Wales. And after co-owners Julian Jenkins and Canva founder Damien Singh got involved before the 2024-25 season, there was hope of keeping some of that emerging talent within Wales while allowing Gwalia to compete at a higher level. However, making progress has not been easy, even if last season's relegation from the Southern Premier Division was the result of fine margins. Gwalia finished with the same goal difference as AFC Wimbledon, but were relegated as the London club had scored one more goal. "It hit us hard, it really did," says manager Cori Williams-Mills. Gwalia are currently fourth in Division One South West, having lost only one of their eight league games so far this season. The average age of the squad is just 20, and Williams-Mills believes her youthful team can not only return to the third tier but go on to reach new heights. "When we get back up, we'll be better equipped than we would have been if we'd stayed [up]," she adds. "Sometimes taking a step back can help push you further forward. "We ended last year a little disappointed. This season, the girls have been excellent. "Is it going to take us time to get where we want to be? Is it going to be hard along the way? ESPN’s Jeff Passan reported the breaking deal between Bauers and Boston, noting that the Red Sox were seeking offensive depth and had found their man early in the offseason. Fans shared blunt reactions to the blockbuster deal on social media. “This is a massive overpay for a guy who could easily put up 0.0 WAR or less in those 4 years. Good for Bauers getting his bag! His career WAR over 5 seasons coming into 2026 was -1.2,” one fan commented. Comment by u/Turbostrider27 from discussion in baseball “Sad to see Jake go but this was predictable,” another said. Bauers set career highs this season, batting .266/.389/.484 with a team-best 26 homers and 86 RBIs. He ranked third in MLB in on-base percentage and sixth in wOBA, while setting personal bests in hits (127), runs (93), walks (94), OPS (.874), and extra-base hits (50). He couldn’t carry that offensive momentum into the postseason, going 9-for-47 with a home run and six RBIs, striking out 19 times, and posting a .621 OPS in 13 playoff games. Despite the postseason slump, it was an impressive season for a slugger who had nearly retired after the 2024 campaign. Where Could Jake Bauers Fit on the Red Sox Roster? Boston already has an All-Star first baseman in Willson Contreras, who led the team in offensive stats in 2026. The 2016 World Series champion with the Chicago Cubs has one season left on his Red Sox contract, and the club intends to keep its star slugger for 2027. Despite Contreras, signing Bauers is a welcome addition for Beantown . The 2026 Fall Classic champion brings on-base ability and power and could fill the lineup’s DH spot. Boston ranked 23rd in runs scored and was swept by the Yankees in the ALWCS, scoring just twice in two games. After a breakout year in 2026, it will be interesting to see how Boston uses the 31-year-old’s talent as the front office continues its effort to revamp the roster to better contend for the championship next season. sports.title: “It’s Disgusting”: Craig Carton Slams Kirk Herbstreit for Feeding Steak to His Dog at NYC Restaurant
sports.description: Kirk Herbstreit gives some love to his dog, Peter. © USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Kirk Herbstreit’s recent outing with his dog Peter has sparked controversy. The ESPN college football analyst shared a video of his dog enjoying a steak at a New York City restaurant. While the moment seemed cute to Herbstreit, sports commentator Craig Carton was not happy about it. He questioned the decision to bring a dog into a steakhouse and feed it a meal meant for humans. Herbstreit posted a video of himself cutting a steak and placing the pieces in front of Peter. The golden retriever wasted no time in finishing the meal, eating an entire plate of cut-up steak in less than 17 seconds. “Petey got into another steak in NYC last night… I wish he would enjoy it,” Herbstreit wrote. However, Carton reacted very differently when discussing the video on his show. “I’m not anti-dog. I just don’t want to go to a steakhouse and eat next to a dog. Because it’s disgusting,” Carton said. He went on to criticize Herbstreit for documenting the experience and questioned why the analyst would serve an expensive steak to his dog while dining with his wife and friends. “‘I love my dog more than you love your dog. You look to your right, and a beautifully cooked medium-rare steak is delivered to the Herbstreit table, but it’s not for any of the adults at that table, it’s for his dog. And Kirk, on camera now, because you’ve got to document everything you do, God forbid you act like a human being and you don’t film every aspect of your life – in a New York City steakhouse,” he added. According to Carton, other customers expecting a quiet meal may have been disturbed by a dog sitting next to them. Kirk Herbstreit’s Dog Peter Continues Ben’s Legacy Peter always accompanies Herbstreit during his college football travels. The golden retriever took on that role after the analyst lost his previous dog, Ben, in November 2024. On November 7, Herbstreit announced the second anniversary of Ben’s passing with an emotional Instagram tribute. “2 years ago today, we lost our beloved Ben. He spread his love across the country and so many of you welcomed him into your lives. We miss him every day and are so appreciative of his spirit that blessed so many lives for the 10 years he was alive. Love you Benny,” Herbstreit wrote. The tribute received an outpouring of affection from fans. Many remembered Ben fondly, while others showered the dog with praise. sports.title: ‘It shows’: Victor Wembanyama has a message to teams planning to be overly physical against him
sports.description: Photo by Alex Goodlett/Getty Images The San Antonio Spurs picked up a dominant 38-point win against the Golden State Warriors. Victor Wembanyama is usually the star of the show for the Spurs, but it was Stephon Castle who impressed the most with 32 points, five rebounds and six assists. The French superstar played his part too, even though Draymond Green and the rest of the Warriors tried to be a bit too physical against him. That, according to Wembanyama, was not a good tactic. Victor Wembanyama says teams being overly physical with him is bad basketball strategy Wembanyama is a force to be reckoned with. The 22-year-old is one of the best players in the NBA, and on his day, he can be absolutely unstoppable going forward. In theory, some people think being very physical with Wembanyama is the way to stop him, and the Warriors, led by Green, tried that on Friday night. Yet, the Frenchman finished the game with 12 points, 12 rebounds, six assists, a steal and two blocks in just 21 minutes. After the game, Wembanyama addressed the physicality and claimed that it was poor strategy. He also claimed that he is ready to sacrifice himself against overly physical teams if it means the Spurs win big – just like they did against the Warriors. He said in a press conference: “No, I feel very secure. I know I have to be smart, but I feel very secure. It’s not a good basketball strategy, and it shows. “So I’m ready to put my body on the line for the team if that allows us to win by 40.” When asked for a response to Green’s shove on him, Wembanyama replied: “Do I have any thoughts on it? Not much. It’s not surprising.” Physicality alone is not enough to stop Wembanyama and the Spurs, who showed on Friday night that they can get the job done even when their star man is limited to just 12 points. The Spurs are comfortably the best team in the NBA right now, and if they keep performing in the same way, they should be able to go all the way this season. sports.title: Thibaut Courtois targeting SHOCK takeover of Italian club as Real Madrid star expands business empire
sports.description: Real Madrid v Sevilla FC - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois is looking to expand his growing business portfolio by launching a takeover bid for Serie C side Reggiana. The Belgium international’s investment fund, NXTPLAY Capital, has presented a proposal to purchase a hundred per cent of the Italian club's shares. Courtois plots Italian takeover bid Courtois could soon become the owner of an Italian football team. His investment fund, NXTPLAY Capital, has officially made an offer to purchase Serie C side Reggiana. According to multiple reports in Italy, including Sky Sport Italia and La Gazzetta dello Sport , the fund has presented a formal proposal. Their ambitious aim is to acquire 100 per cent of the club's shares and assume complete control. The move marks a significant step into sports ownership for the veteran shot-stopper. He is actively looking to expand his business influence while continuing his playing career in Spain. Building a club for the community Courtois formed NXTPLAY Capital alongside his business partner Gonzalo Vila in 2025. The private equity fund focuses heavily on strategic investments across sports, media, technology, and consumer brands. The Madrid star has outlined a clear vision for the Italian outfit, promising deep local integration. "We want to build something the people of Reggio Emilia can be proud of: ambitious on the field, close to the community, and built to last," explained Courtois. Developing local talent is also a massive priority for the new project in Italy. "Giving young players the right environment to grow in will be at the centre of everything we do," he added. Growing a vast sports portfolio If this takeover is successful, Reggiana will not be the first football club in NXTPLAY Capital’s growing portfolio. The fund already holds strategic investments in other European teams. They currently have financial stakes in French side Le Mans FC and Belgian outfit KRC Genk. Courtois and Vila are actively using these strategic investments to build a wider network of clubs. Adding a historic Italian side to that network represents a major statement of intent from the Belgian goalkeeper. Reggiana currently compete in Serie C, but fresh financial backing could help push them forward. Awaiting an official binding offer Despite the clear interest from Courtois and his partners, the exact status of the takeover negotiations remains slightly uncertain. Current Reggiana owner Romano Amadei has publicly clarified the situation regarding the sale. Amadei confirmed that while NXTPLAY Capital are highly interested, the current board has yet to receive a fully binding offer for the football club. The Italian side's leadership is proceeding carefully.

technology.title: Microsoft's school email bill gives rivals something to smile about
technology.description: The fallout from Microsoft's education price rises and service cuts continues as institutions weigh the prospect of bigger bills, and the Windows maker's rivals struggle not to pull "I told you so" faces. The main takeaways are that free student email and collaboration services are being retired, and storage entitlements are changing. These changes generally apply at institutions' first renewal or extension on or after January 1, 2028. Microsoft announced the new plans last week, and the UK's Department for Education described itself as "disappointed" at the news. As well it might be, although the UK government has rarely seen a deal from Microsoft that it didn't like . Or, for that matter, other US tech giants . Exactly how much educational institutions will have to spend remains unclear. Mary Jo Foley of Directions on Microsoft put indicative student pricing at $2 per year for Microsoft 365 Education A2, $4 for A3, and $6 for A5, with Teams adding another dollar annually. Faculty licenses cost considerably more, while the new A7 student tier jumps to $385 a year before Teams. Foley cautioned that these were approximate figures, with actual prices set by Microsoft's partners. The new no-cost student tier, Microsoft 365 Education A0, is a poor replacement for Office 365 A1: it excludes Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and Teams. Eligibility also requires full paid faculty coverage on A2 or higher and students who actively use Windows devices for education – potentially awkward for institutions running fleets of Chromebooks. A few dollars per student might not sound alarming. Multiply that across an institution, however, and something that used to be free becomes a recurring bill. Michael Meeks, CEO of Collabora Productivity, told The Register: "Free was the bait on the hook, and Microsoft spent years reeling in schools' email accounts, documents, identity management and classrooms onto its cloud." A poster on the edugeek.net forums commented: "This was always going to happen, I remember thinking this when we moved over to the MS free cloud solution. It will be free until they decide it isn't." The risk for Microsoft is that there are options. Meeks told us: "Schools now have a year to plan, and, in our experience with other large-scale educational projects, such as the University of Lille, that can be enough time to migrate properly." Other options include Nextcloud, which will be rolled out as part of Germany's Educational Cloud Infrastructure . Several Swiss universities also migrated to the service over an August weekend. According to Nextcloud, 39,500 students, teachers, and researchers, along with 585 terabytes of data, were shifted. Both Nextcloud and Collabora Productivity also highlight another factor that could drive educational institutions away from Microsoft: sovereignty. technology.title: Big Tech takes a beating as online safety experts accuse companies of doing bare minimum
technology.description: Technology companies are doing just enough to show a degree of compliance with the UK's Online Safety Act, but are failing to meet the needs of the individuals and young victims the legislation exists to protect, experts say. A panel of online safety pros assembled before Parliament's Communications and Digital Committee on Tuesday, taking aim at the likes of Google, Microsoft, Meta, and ByteDance for failing to act on important matters. Clare McGlynn, professor of law at Durham University and expert on violence against women and girls (VAWG), was especially critical of major search engine providers for their inconsistent downranking of harmful content search terms. "Rape porn," for example, is correctly downranked and no user sees any relevant links until the tenth page of results, although adjacent terms such as "unwilling porn" can be found as early as the third page, McGlynn said. "I just think if someone spent a little more time thinking 'I really want to minimize the risk of this material appearing,' I would take a systematic approach," she told the committee. "I would downrank 'unwilling' and 'unwanted,' and I would downrank 'asleep porn' as well… because it just means that it's easily findable. "So, they don't rank some of them, but just not systematically or wholly consistently." McGlynn went on to say that during her own research, "force porn" was rightly downranked heavily, although terms as similar as "forced porn" were not. "If you were trying to think of the words that would be similar to say rape, and rape porn is extreme porn and it's not supposed to be on those platforms anymore, you would think of words like unwilling and unwanted," she added. "And we know your algorithm would." Google inevitably took much of McGlynn's flak due to its dominance of the search engine market, although the professor said the same issues can be observed on Bing, too. Alexandra Whiston-Dew, partner at law firm Miscon de Raya, argued that search engines have such an important role in regulating the OSA, noting the limited resources at Ofcom's disposal. She said that more needs to be done from the tech side to ensure different parties in the chain of publication are detected early and downranked or blocked accordingly. There are publications, for example, that actively advertise themselves as websites that host illegal content, and these appear to be missing from the search engines' crosshairs. "So, they are spotlighting the fact that they are publishing illegal content, and this is going under the radar not only from the search engines but also the other platforms and the businesses in the chain of publication," said Whiston-Dew. "Also Ofcom needs to really pull all of their resources together and attack that receptacle of illegal content." Conditions were ideal for the launch, with the atmospheric winds so calm the rocket’s white plume did not dissipate for many minutes. The weather in South Texas is not always comfortable; summers are long and hot. Friday evening was perfect at Starbase. The first stage ascended toward space flawlessly, releasing the upper stage above the Gulf of Mexico. technology.title: Millions of Americans are not taking their GLP-1 drugs as prescribed
technology.description: GLP-1 medications are everywhere these days. The peptide-based drugs are both highly effective and wildly popular for diabetes, weight loss and a growing range of connected chronic health conditions, including cardiovascular disease and obstructive sleep apnea. But, amid the boom, the latest data suggests millions of Americans have turned to unapproved versions and are using the potent drugs in ways doctors never intended, raising questions about what that real-world use means for safety and efficacy. In a study published this week , researchers at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention broke down survey data of GLP-1 use collected between July and August of 2025. Based on responses from over 8,000 US adults, the researchers estimate that about one in 10 US adults (9.8 percent) used a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, aka GLP-1 medication, in 2025. That's around 27 million adults. The study was published in the CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. Among GLP-1 users, nearly half (44 percent) reported using their GLP-1 in a way that was different from how it was prescribed. Users skipped doses, delayed getting refills, and used smaller doses than prescribed, among other changes. More than half of the people modifying how they used the drug said the changes were because of cost or availability reasons. Cost and access barriers were most pronounced among younger GLP-1 users. Fifty-eight percent of adults 14­–39 years old who modified their use cited cost as a barrier, compared with just 20 percent of adults 65 or older who said the same. Read full article Comments

technology.title: Chinese AI labs are training models on Nvidia's Blackwell despite export controls, says ex-OpenAI engineer
technology.description: US export controls are not stopping AI labs in China from using restricted Nvidia chips, according to a report from a former OpenAI engineer. Will DePue, who left the AI giant earlier this year to launch Unemployment Labs, an AI research consultancy, published forensic evidence showing that "DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group have gained access to Nvidia's Blackwell GPUs, despite restrictions on exporting these chips to China, and are using that hardware to create their AI models." "This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it," said DePue in a social media post . "When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern – a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model." It doesn't sound that insane. The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang followed from revelations that he had an affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who, in 2023, founded Singapore-based Megaspeed International. That company is reportedly under investigation by US authorities for allegedly smuggling Nvidia chips to China. Huang's departure coincides with a renewed push to tighten US chip export controls. House Speaker Mike Johnson supports the idea . And there are at least four bills awaiting consideration that aim to limit China's access to leading edge AI tech: the AI Overwatch Act, the Chip Security Act, Match Act, and the Cloud Security Act. On Monday, US Senators Jim Banks (R-Ind.) and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) cited Jensen Huang's "relationship with a suspected Chinese spy" as a justification for passing the AI Overwatch Act, which would codify the Trump administration's existing chip export controls. The Trump administration on Thursday said it's not sure whether Alice Huang was a spy, an allegation denied by Beijing and currently under investigation by the FBI. Whatever the case, the current rules clearly are not working. Only a few weeks ago, Lava, an Israel-based security company, said it had found "32 Nvidia B300 GPUs, part of Nvidia's Blackwell Ultra generation, through publicly exposed monitoring endpoints with IP addresses geolocated to China." These GPUs, Lava noted, are subject to US export controls [PDF]. The security biz said its findings followed from the exposure of monitoring systems intended for internal infrastructure management that were publicly exposed. How DePue reached his conclusion The analysis published through DePue's consultancy, "Top Chinese Frontier AI Models Carry the Fingerprint of Export-Controlled Nvidia Blackwell GPUs," takes a different approach: analyzing the published weights of various models from Chinese AI labs. technology.title: This year’s bug count just passed 100K
technology.description: Chalk up a new record for vulns. The number of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) found and disclosed so far in 2026 surpassed 100,000 on Friday - more than double 2025’s total - and the reason can be summed up in two letters: AI. “It’s kind of wild,” Josh Bressers, VulnCheck’s director of coordinated vulnerability disclosure, told The Register . “The thing that almost scares the bejesus out of me is while 100K sounds like a lot, in a couple years we're going to say, remember when it was only 100K?” As of the time of our interview, about 4 pm UTC on Friday, VulnCheck counted 100,222 CVEs, he said. Microsoft alone added 1,094 security flaws to the total count on Tuesday, following 1,474 vulnerabilities the month before. “There's no denying the fact that vulnerability hunting with AI is driving a majority of what we're seeing.” All the major CVE Numbering Authorities (CNAs) - these are the organizations authorized by the CVE program to assign unique identifiers to security vulnerabilities - like VulnCheck, Microsoft, Oracle, GitHub, and other large enterprise IT vendors “are just screaming into the atmosphere right now,” Bressers said. “It’s AI.” Meanwhile, the percentage of these bugs that are exploited in the wild remains relatively consistent. About 1.4 percent (1,363) of the CVEs published this year have been added to VulnCheck’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. “But obviously, as the number of CVEs grows, [1 percent] of 1,000 is a lot different than [1 percent] of 100,000,” Bressers said. Plus, as other security researchers have documented, the window between the public release of a security patch and attackers developing working exploits – often by reverse engineering the patch while end users are still applying the fix – is rapidly shrinking. This is also thanks to AI . From CVE to KEV From January to June, 88 percent of the exploitation observed by CrowdStrike using public proof-of-concept (PoC) code occurred within 48 hours of the code's release. The security firm said China-linked groups such as Vault Panda and Genesis Panda moved even faster, launching attacks within 24 hours of disclosure. Similarly, VulnCheck found the median time from CVE publication to exploitation falling from 120 days in 2025 to 80 days during the first half of 2026. technology.title: Meatbags suck at spotting lying LLMs, so let AI narc on itself
technology.description: The internet is full of schlock, from biased news and dubious hot takes to false factoids. LogicLens aims to separate fact from fiction using the very same technology behind some of that slop: AI. It’s a simple premise, really: LogicLens, which lives in Chrome as a browser extension , or on iOS in the form of a mobile app called Receipts , combs through articles, social media posts, and other content to check it not only for factual inaccuracies, but also for bad reasoning. LogicLens and Receipts claim to identify logical fallacies , flag reports that misrepresent information, detect content that attempts to polarize an issue, and the like. It also cites sources, so if, for example, you need to call someone out on their BS, you’ll have ammunition. Or, if you’re trying to fact-check something before sharing it, you can get a more accurate view of the situation, and maybe post something else instead. Using the Chrome extension is as simple as clicking on its icon in the list of extensions in the browser. On iOS, the Receipts app is found as a share option. Once it starts, LogicLens scans an article, post, video, etc. to find potential issues of factual or logical inconsistency and flags them for review. If the facts of the matter turn out to contradict your worldview, LogicLens’ creators say they’re not trying to be partisan - you may just not be as informed as you need to be, which hopefully their tool will assist with. “We're not trying to be the referee of truth,” the company’s about page states. “Instead, LogicLens helps uncover the context, so you can decide for yourself without the spin." Of course, AI is increasingly used for online analysis and content review, and LogicLens is no exception. LogicLens doesn't identify the AI models powering its service in its publicly available documentation, but AI is definitely the backbone of the system. According to LogicLens, it's using an AI system that's “Research-backed and custom designed to outperform general models like ChatGPT & even trained experts.” We’ll leave that up to anyone willing to give the tool a spin to decide, but one thing’s for certain: The world needs something. Large language models and image generation tools are increasingly being used to generate internet content slop, and not all of it is as harmless as poorly made commercials for drop-shipped garbage: Some of it is being used to craft very convincing misinformation.
